server.name: gitcafe
server.title: GitCafe
server.description: Read public repository code, issues and pull requests; sign in with OAuth to manage them.

live.instructions:
GitCafe is a Git forge. This session is not signed in: read tools cover public repositories only, and private repositories look the same as missing ones. list_repositories needs an owner or topic.

Write tools and get_me return HTTP 401 so the client can sign in with OAuth. A connection also reads the private repositories the user approves: https://staging.git.cafe/docs/account/mcp-connections.md

Authentication options: https://staging.git.cafe/docs/agent-workflows.md#choose-how-to-authenticate

tools.name: get_me
tools.title: Get signed-in user
tools.description: Read who this connection is signed in as and what it may reach: your actor identity and, for an OAuth connection, the repositories and permissions the user approved and when it expires. Returns null when the credential names no user. Call it first to learn which repositories the other tools can reach: every repository the user can access, or the ones they selected (adding one to a selection needs the user to connect again).

actorId.description: The signed-in user's ID (act_...); pass it in assigneeIds to assign yourself.

handle.description: Your handle, as shown in GitCafe.

displayName.description: Your display name; null when none is set.

avatarUrl.description: URL of your avatar image; null when there is none.

allRepositories.description: true when the user approved every repository they can access, including ones created or shared with them later; repositories is then empty.

repositories.description: The repositories this connection may use, as owner/repo, when the user selected them; empty when allRepositories is true.

permissions.description: The permissions the user approved, as kind:family:level, e.g. pr:contents:write.

expiresAt.description: When this connection ends unless used again (each token refresh moves it to 90 days out) and its tokens stop working, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC.

connection.description: What this OAuth connection may reach; null for a session or token credential.

result.description: The signed-in user and their connection, or null when the credential names no user.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.title: List repositories
tools.description: List the repositories this connection can read, oldest first, one page at a time, narrowed by owner, topic or name prefix (filters combine). Signed in, it lists the approved repositories; without sign-in it lists public repositories only, needs owner or topic, and q is not available. Pass an item's owner and name to the other tools.

limit.description: How many repositories to return in this page; omit for the default page size.

owner.description: Only repositories owned by this user or organization, by handle (acme for acme/website). Combines with topic and q: a repository must match every filter given.

q.description: Only repositories whose name starts with this text, ignoring case. Needs sign-in; combines with owner and topic.

topic.description: Only repositories tagged with this topic, e.g. rust. Combines with owner and q.

after.description: The next cursor from the previous page, to continue the list; omit for the first page.

id.description: The repository's ID (repo_...); pass it as create_pull_request sourceRepo.

owner.description: Handle of the user or organization that owns the repository: the owner argument of the other tools.

name.description: The repository's name: the repo argument of the other tools.

description.description: The repository's description; null when none is set.

homepage.description: The repository's homepage URL; null when none is set.

topics.description: The topics the repository is tagged with.

visibility.description: public: anyone can read it. private: only members and connections the owner approved.

defaultBranch.description: Short name of the default branch, e.g. main.

archivedAt.description: When the repository was archived (made read-only), as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; null while it is active.

updatedAt.description: When the repository was last changed, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC.

items.description: The repositories in this page.

next.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; pass it as after. null on the last page.

result.description: One page of repositories.

tools.name: list_refs
tools.title: List branches or tags
tools.description: List a repository's branches or its tags, sorted by name, one page at a time, optionally narrowed by a name substring. Each ref carries the commit it points to and, for an annotated tag, its signature check. Pass a ref's name as ref to list_tree, read_file or search_code, or its target commit's oid as oid to pin later reads to one commit.

limit.description: How many refs to return in this page; omit for the default page size.

name.description: Short name of the branch or tag, e.g. main or v1.0; pass it as ref.

oid.description: The ref's own object ID: the commit for a branch or lightweight tag, the tag object for an annotated tag.

tools.name: list_tree
tools.title: List repository directory
tools.description: List the entries of one directory of a repository, not recursively, at a branch, tag or commit, one page at a time; later pages stay on the same commit. Each entry says whether it is a file, directory, submodule or symbolic link. Omit path for the root; pass a tree's path back to descend and a blob's path to read_file.

repo.description: The repository's name within that owner: website for the repository acme/website. list_repositories and get_repository return both parts.

oid.description: The exact commit to read, as a 40-character hexadecimal OID; takes precedence over ref. Use it to keep several reads on one commit.

path.description: The directory to list, by its path from the repository root, e.g. src/mcp; omit for the root.

after.description: The next cursor from the previous page, to continue the listing on the same commit; omit for the first page.

limit.description: How many entries to return in this page; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_file
tools.title: Read repository file
tools.description: Read one file of a repository at a branch, tag or commit, a window of lines at a time. A text file comes with its line window and nextLine to continue; a binary file comes with null content. A window holds at most maxLines lines and 64 KiB; a file over 1 MiB cannot be read. Take path from list_tree or search_code.

owner.description: The user or organization that owns the repository: acme for the repository acme/website.

repo.description: The repository's name within that owner: website for the repository acme/website. list_repositories and get_repository return both parts.

ref.description: The revision to read: a branch or tag name from list_refs, a full ref such as refs/heads/main or refs/tags/v1, HEAD (the default branch), or a commit OID. Use the full ref when a branch and a tag share a name. Ignored when oid is set.

oid.description: The exact commit to read, as a 40-character hexadecimal OID; takes precedence over ref. Use it to keep several reads on one commit.

result.description: One window of a file.

tools.name: search_code
tools.title: Search repository code
tools.description: Search the text files of a repository at a branch, tag or commit for a literal string, optionally within one file or directory. tools.description: Merge a pull request into its target branch with an explicit strategy, at the exact head, base and version you reviewed. tools.description: Submit a review of a pull request at an exact commit and version: approve, request changes, or comment without a decision, with an optional overall body. visibility.description: public: anyone can read it. private: only members and connections the owner approved.

defaultBranch.description: Short name of the default branch, e.g. main.

Pass a ref's name as ref to list_tree, read_file or search_code, or its target commit's oid as oid to pin later reads to one commit.

search.description: Only refs whose name contains this text, ignoring case; omit for every ref.

after.description: The next cursor from the previous page, to continue the list; omit for the first page.

limit.description: How many refs to return in this page; omit for the default page size.

name.description: Short name of the branch or tag, e.g. main or v1.0; pass it as ref.

oid.description: The ref's own object ID: the commit for a branch or lightweight tag, the tag object for an annotated tag.

isHead.description: true for the default branch, false for every other ref.

annotated.description: true for an annotated tag, false for a branch or lightweight tag.

oid.description: The commit, as a commit OID.

summary.description: First line of the commit message.

name.description: The author's name.

signer.description: Who signed it; null unless reason is valid.

tools.name: list_tree
tools.title: List repository directory
tools.description: List the entries of one directory of a repository, not recursively, at a branch, tag or commit, one page at a time; later pages stay on the same commit. Each entry says whether it is a file, directory, submodule or symbolic link. Omit path for the root; pass a tree's path back to descend and a blob's path to read_file.

repo.description: The repository's name within that owner: website for the repository acme/website. list_repositories and get_repository return both parts.

repo.description: The repository's name within that owner: website for the repository acme/website. list_repositories and get_repository return both parts.

facet.description: detail: the pull request, with its version, headOid, observedBaseOid, mergeRoute and your capabilities. reviews: one page of submitted reviews, oldest first. commits: one page of its commits, newest first. files: one page of changed files, whose paths get_pull_request_diff reads. status: merge readiness and checks, with the version, headOid and baseOid merge_pull_request needs. comments: one page of conversation and inline comments, with IDs, thread IDs and versions. merge_status: the state of a merge, identified by operationId.

limit.description: How many reviews, commits, files or comments to return in this page; other facets ignore it.

operationId.description: For merge_status: the id returned by merge_pull_request.

id.description: The merge operation's ID (prmop_... for a native merge, ghd_... for a GitHub merge); pass it as operationId to pull_request_read facet merge_status to follow it.

state.description: accepted: admitted, still running or waiting; not merged yet. completed: merged. failed: not merged, and this operation will not merge.

resultOid.description: The target branch's commit after the merge, as a commit OID; present once the merge completed.

reason.description: Why the merge failed or is waiting; absent when completed. rejected: refused before starting. merge-precondition-changed: head, base or version no longer match. native-conflict: the branches conflict. native-failure: the merge could not be written. native-cancelled: cancelled. reconciliation-required: the recorded state must be reconciled first. already-up-to-date: nothing to merge.

attempts.description: How many times the merge has been attempted; present when reading an operation.

anyOf.description: For facet merge_status: the merge operation's outcome so far. Treat only state completed as merged.

id.description: The pull request's ID (pr_...).

version.description: The pull request's current version; pass it as expectedVersion to merge_pull_request.

tools.description: Read the patch of chosen changed files of a pull request, pinned to the version the files were listed at. Each file comes with its hunks and line origins; a binary or too-large file has no hunks, and hunksOmitted marks a file whose hunks did not fit the response, so request fewer paths. Take paths and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet files; the line numbers are what add_comment target pull_inline anchors to.

tools.name: submit_review

tools.description: Submit a review of a pull request at an exact commit and version: approve, request changes, or comment without a decision, with an optional overall body. Returns the review with its id, verdict and commit. Take commitOid (headOid) and expectedVersion from pull_request_read facet detail or status; the review fails if the pull request changed since, so read again and resubmit at the new head. To publish a draft review you saved in the GitCafe web UI, with its inline comments, pass its id and version as draft with the same verdict, body and commit it was saved with; these tools cannot create or read drafts. tools.description: Send a report about GitCafe itself to the GitCafe team: a tool that failed or misbehaved, a confusing result, or a missing capability.
